# Coherent projective charts: no cycles and an exact entropy decomposition

This uses the actual source-face charts and unchanged rows in
source-face-common-projective-chart-and-exact-row-tilt-identities-optimal-midpoint.md.
the contributor and Optimal-midpoint independently obtained the same explicit
chart scaling. It is not an assumption that independently chosen
source charts can be compared without a loss.

## 1. The intrinsic concave profile

Write

    F(z,x)=E_(C_z)(x)^(1/d),   v(z)=|C_z|^(1/d),
    Psi(z,x)=F(z,x)^(d/(d+1)) v(z)^(1/(d+1))
            =[E_(C_z)(x)|C_z|^(1/d)]^(1/(d+1)).          (1)

The weighted geometric mean is increasing and concave on positive
arguments. Since F and v are concave, Psi is concave on the
interior-fiber domain. It extends continuously by zero at marked
fiber boundary points where energy vanishes. Its physical dimension
is length: both F and v have that dimension.

At an interior mark Y_i=(p_i,y_i), let a_i be its ordinary optimizing
projective parameter. The proved energy envelope derivative gives

    grad_x F(Y_i)=((d+1)/d) F(Y_i) a_i,
    grad_x Psi(Y_i)=Psi(Y_i) a_i.                       (2)

Thus the normalized continuous tangent of this ONE intrinsic
concave profile is exactly the centroidal projective normalizer.

## 2. Explicit comparison between every pair of source faces

For each occupied source face Q use the genuine chart W_Q from
the preceding note. It touches L at every source in Q. Define the
positive constants, independent of the chosen source i on Q,

    kappa_Q=F_i/L_i,    upsilon_Q=v_i/L_i,
    b_Q=kappa_Q^(d/(d+1)) upsilon_Q^(1/(d+1)).           (3)

Their constancy follows from actual pointed homothety with scale L.
For an arbitrary positive source i, belonging to some face R,
the global energy and volume-root majorants defining W_Q give

    W_Q(Y_i)/L_i
       >= [d/(d+1)] kappa_R/kappa_Q
                      +[1/(d+1)] upsilon_R/upsilon_Q
       >= b_R/b_Q.                                    (4)

The last inequality is weighted arithmetic--geometric mean.
In particular, every cyclic product of the cross-face lower bounds
is at least one. The source-ownership difference constraints have
the EXPLICIT positive solution obtained by multiplying chart Q
by b_Q; no Perron--Frobenius existence claim is needed.

Let

    G_Q=b_Q W_Q,       U=min_Q G_Q.                     (5)

Then for every original positive source i,

    U(Y_i)=b_Q L_i=Psi(Y_i) when i belongs to Q.          (6)

If a source belongs to several faces their b_Q values coincide,
so this is unambiguous. Other source charts cannot undershoot this
value. Thus the lower envelope retains each face's own source
contact after the prescribed scaling.

Globally each G_Q majorizes Psi. To see the constants exactly,
choose a reference source j on Q, let S_Q>=F and T_Q>=v be the
energy and volume-root affine supports used to construct its
chart, and write

    G_Q=Psi(Y_j)
          [d S_Q/((d+1)F_j)+T_Q/((d+1)v_j)].             (7)

Weighted arithmetic--geometric mean, followed by S_Q>=F and T_Q>=v,
gives G_Q>=Psi. Therefore U is a positive concave PL majorant of
Psi touching every original positive source. Each G_Q remains a
genuine centroidal projective chart when normalized at its source.

## 3. Exact parameter slack = chart entropy + envelope competition

Assign each old WHOLE source row to one touching face, as in the
preceding note. Retain

    eta_Q=L nu_Q,   hat_eta_Q=W_Q nu_Q,
    eta_Q(C)=hat_eta_Q(C)=s_Q,
    sum_Q eta_Q=dm/M.

The relative entropy D(eta_Q||hat_eta_Q) equals
-integral log(W_Q/L)d eta_Q. On all sources assigned to Q,
Psi(Y_i)/L_i=b_Q. Consequently the exact identity is

    Delta_U
      :=sum_i sigma_i log[Psi(Y_i)/L_i]
                          -(1/M)integral log(U/L)dm
       =sum_Q D(eta_Q||hat_eta_Q)
                     +sum_Q integral log(G_Q/U)d eta_Q. (8)

Indeed G_Q=b_Q W_Q, and integrating its logarithm against eta_Q
gives s_Q log b_Q minus the first entropy term. Subtract the
logarithm of U and sum the exact original-volume allocation.

Every term on the right is nonnegative. The old global parameter
certificate asserts Delta_U>=0, but (8) shows why that inequality
alone does NOT force equality. It is already explained by the
mean-one chart ratios and lower-envelope competition.

Similarly,

    Delta_Psi
      :=sum_i sigma_i log[Psi(Y_i)/L_i]
                          -(1/M)integral log(Psi/L)dm
       =Delta_U+(1/M)integral log(U/Psi)dm.             (9)

These integrals are finite at a fixed positive canonical body.
For the potentially vanishing Psi, energy monotonicity applied to
the ball of radius dist(x,partial K_z) about x gives
E_(K_z)(x)>=omega_d dist(x,partial K_z)^d, while E<=|K_z|.
The logarithm of distance is integrable in a convex body with
positive inradius, by the O(delta) bound on its inner boundary
collar. There are only finitely many fibers.

Equality in (9) would force, on each allocated row,

    W_Q=L and G_Q=U=Psi almost everywhere.              (10)

The same equality in (8) forces the first two identities, with
G_Q=U but without necessarily U=Psi. Such identities would be
substantial new contact rigidity. No existing parameter-only
certificate forces their equality; an additional actual body
variational argument would be needed.

## 4. A full inverse-moment family, with the same limitation

For every p>0,

    (1/M)integral (L/U)^p dm
                  >=sum_i sigma_i [L_i/Psi(Y_i)]^p.    (11)

One direct proof uses the SAME row ratios g_Q=W_Q/L. Since U<=b_Q W_Q,

    integral (L/U)^p d eta_Q
       >=b_Q^(-p) integral g_Q^(-p)d eta_Q
       >=b_Q^(-p) s_Q,

where the second inequality is Jensen and integral g_Q d eta_Q=s_Q.
Summation proves (11). Thus these moment constraints alone cannot
eliminate the entropy defects either.

For comparison, (11) also comes from an actual legal concave
parameter path:

    V_t=(L^(-p)+t U^(-p))^(-1/p),       t>=0.             (12)

The function (x^(-p)+t y^(-p))^(-1/p) is increasing and concave
for positive x,y. Its Hessian is

    -(p+1)t S^(-1/p-2) x^(-p-2)y^(-p-2)
                    [[y^2,-xy],[-xy,x^2]],
    S=x^(-p)+t y^(-p),

which is negative semidefinite. Therefore (12) is concave and
positive. The fixed-row logarithmic certificate applied to V_t
and differentiated at zero yields (11), since
d(log V_t)/dt|0=-(L/U)^p/p. This is a genuine path, not a presumed
two-sided parameter variation.

## 5. Uniform chart floors independent of the free parameter

Formula (7) has a useful application that does not use the old
parameter L or its rows at all. For ANY interior mark Y of a
canonical positive family, choose affine supports S>=F and T>=v
touching there and define G by (7). Then

    G/Psi(Y)>= min_(z in B)v(z)/[(d+1)v(p)]>0            (13)

on the whole canonical body: S>=0 on its closure and T>=v.
If all real fibers have a common inner radius r and outer radius
R, the right side is at least r/[(d+1)R].

The normalized continuous gradient is exactly a_Y by (2).
On a compact class with fixed finite base, uniform inner/outer
fiber bounds, and marks in a uniform own-fiber interior core,
the finite-hull support arguments give bounded choices of S,T
and hence bounded chart coefficients. The energy minimizer is
bounded by the reciprocal source-core radius. The positive
floor (13) is uniform over that class.

These facts apply to a NEW body-tied buffer built from Psi without
importing a free-parameter transport certificate into its different
variational cone. They supply coherent positive charts and ordinary
own-source projective cap credit, but do not by themselves supply
its physical separator or outside-contact cost identity.
